Marc / Sofia / Jonas — attaching our proposed redline (we converted key points into two alternative paragraphs so procurement can pick a preferred path). Summary of our proposals:

1) Third-party IP claims — primary option: Redwood retains right to defend and control litigation, Redwood will pay defense costs and any settlement up to the capped indemnity amount. If Redwood declines to defend (rare), Redwood will reimburse documented defense costs subject to the cap.

2) Evidence custody & retention — we agree to a documented handoff process for logs and artifacts. Redwood commits to preserve ephemeral inference logs for 90 days in a searchable archive and will export a forensic bundle within 10 business days on receipt of a valid notice. For longer-term retention (180 days) we can provide export instructions and a recommended manifest; Redwood will not be the long-term custodian unless contracted in order form.

3) Cap — we can accept a reciprocal cap equal to 12x the monthly committed run-rate (or specific negotiated dollar cap). For AI-generated output claims, we propose excluding speculative punitive damages but will consider a limited carve with appropriate insurance proof.

Attached: Redwood-Indemnity-Response.docx (converted into Acme-friendly markup)

Two asks:
- Marc: confirm whether Acme's procurement needs Redwood to be the long-term custodian for 180 days or if an export-within-10-days workflow suffices.
- Jonas / Sofia: if Acme wants Redwood to retain full custody, we need an SOW add-on including storage & access SLA language and an additional fee estimate.
